title: REDUCE: Registry for patients with diagnosed hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy evaluated for myosin-inhibitor therapy
summary: With new medications such as mavacamten, developed specifically for this condition, there is now, for the first time, a targeted treatment option for people with a typically hereditary thickening of the heart muscle known as hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM). The aim of this registry is to gather real-world clinical experience: How effective is the therapy? How safe is it? And what is the actual need for treatment? Included are patients with this heart condition who are either being treated with the new medication, are scheduled for another therapy such as a heart muscle intervention, or do not require further treatment. The study will observe, among other things, the course of the disease, improvements in physical capacity, lab values, heart imaging (e.g., via ultrasound or MRI), and important events such as hospitalizations, arrhythmias, or death.

interventions.name: Patients with the Diagnosis of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients
- with a current or prior diagnosis of hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy (HOCM) according to current guidelines, and
- who have received guideline-based treatment with non-specific negatively inotropic medications and/or have undergone septal reduction therapy, and
- who present at the participating center during the period in which mavacamten was used there as part of the Compassionate Use Program (CUP), or from July 1, 2023, at the latest.
Exclusion criteria:
Participation not desired, no informed consent
